title: The DB is melting
summary: A cache absorbs repeated reads before they reach the database.

lesson.problem: More app servers mean more queries, and they all land on one database. It is now the bottleneck.
why: Most reads ask for the same popular data again and again. An in-memory cache answers those in well under a millisecond and keeps them away from the database.
The common pattern is cache-aside: the app checks the cache first; on a miss it reads the database and writes the result into the cache with a time-to-live (TTL).
A 90% hit ratio means the database sees only a tenth of the reads it used to.
takeaways: Caches trade freshness for speed: decide how stale data may be (TTL) and when to invalidate.
Watch for stampedes: when a hot key expires, many requests may hit the database at once.
The cache is an optimisation; the database stays the source of truth.
